title: The Silicon Valley Tour
desc: Benchmark against FAANG engineering cultures
narrative: You've been sent to the Valley to study how the top companies engineer. You're visiting Google, Meta, and two startups. What do you bring back?

success.text: You adapt the best practices. Team productivity jumps.

failure.text: You copy the worst parts. Team hates the new rituals.

success.text: Your culture is unique and sticky. Top talent wants in.

failure.text: Culture is incoherent. People leave for 'better' places.

success.text: Your offers are competitive. You attract great people.

failure.text: Compensation is too high. Finance pushes back hard.

title: The IPO Preparation
desc: Prepare the engineering org for an IPO
narrative: The company is going public. SEC requires rigorous technical controls. Your engineering processes will be scrutinized by auditors, investors, and the press.

success.text: Audit passes cleanly. Investors are impressed.

failure.text: Process is so heavy that deployments stall. Missed targets.

success.text: Compliance-as-code. Audit is a formality.

failure.text: Automation has blind spots. Audit finds gaps.

success.text: Experts navigate the process smoothly.

failure.text: Experts don't understand your tech. Recommendations are wrong.

title: The Patent War
desc: A competitor sues for patent infringement
narrative: A non-practicing entity (patent troll) has sued your company for $50M. They claim your core feature infringes on their patent. Legal wants you to help defend.

success.text: You find smoking gun prior art. Case dismissed.

failure.text: Prior art is weak. Settlement is expensive.

success.text: Counter-sue lands. They settle quickly.

failure.text: Counter-sue is weak. You look aggressive.

success.text: Settlement is reasonable. No precedent set.

failure.text: Settlement is huge. Sets bad precedent.

title: The Government Contract
desc: Bid on a government technology contract
narrative: The government wants to modernize a legacy system. The contract is massive but comes with security clearances, compliance requirements, and political risk.

success.text: You win the contract. Revenue soars.

failure.text: You lose the bid. Resources were wasted.

success.text: Partner handles compliance. You focus on tech.

failure.text: Partner is slow. You miss deadlines.

success.text: You avoid the risk. No regrets.

failure.text: Competitor wins. They gain government credibility.

title: The Technical Fellow Track
desc: Apply for the company's Technical Fellow program
narrative: The Technical Fellow program is the highest individual contributor track. It's peer-reviewed by existing Fellows. One slot. Three candidates including you.

success.text: Your vision is visionary. You're elected.

failure.text: Presentation is too academic. Fellows want practical.

success.text: You have the votes. Election is a formality.

failure.text: Coalitions fracture. You lose to a rival.

success.text: Your track record speaks. You win.

failure.text: Politics win. Someone with less merit gets it.

title: The Platform Strategy
desc: Decide the company's platform architecture
narrative: The company needs a platform strategy. Build in-house, buy, or open-source? This decision will shape the next decade. The board wants your recommendation.

success.text: In-house platform becomes a competitive moat.

failure.text: In-house platform is over-engineered. Nobody uses it.

success.text: Acquisition accelerates your roadmap by 2 years.

failure.text: Acquisition integration fails. You have two broken systems.

success.text: Open-source platform gains adoption. You lead it.

failure.text: Open-source project stalls. No one maintains it.

title: The Board Seat
desc: You're offered a seat on the company's board
narrative: The board wants you to join as an executive director. You'll have fiduciary duties, access to sensitive information, and ultimate accountability.

success.text: You bring engineering perspective to the board. Trusted.

failure.text: Board sees you as too technical. Your voice is marginalized.

success.text: Observer role gives you insight without obligation.

failure.text: Observer status is seen as weakness. You lose influence.

success.text: You avoid politics. Engineering focus pays off.

failure.text: You're excluded from key decisions. Your team suffers.

title: The Quantum Computing Pivot
desc: Evaluate quantum computing for your domain
narrative: A quantum computing startup wants to partner with you. Quantum could revolutionize your domain — or it could be a decade away from practical use.

success.text: Quantum breakthrough. You're 5 years ahead of competitors.

failure.text: Quantum is still theoretical. You wasted 2 years.

success.text: Team finds a niche application. Patent filed.

failure.text: Team produces nothing. Funding is cut.

success.text: You avoid the risk. When quantum is ready, you'll adapt.

failure.text: Competitor moves first. You're behind.

title: The Regulatory Hearing
desc: Testify before Congress on technology policy
narrative: You've been summoned to testify before Congress on AI regulation. The media will be watching. Your words will shape policy for the next decade.

success.text: Your testimony is quoted in the final bill. Wise regulation.

failure.text: Testimony is misinterpreted. Bad regulation passes.

success.text: Congress appreciates the technical clarity.

failure.text: Congress thinks you're evasive. Media pounces.

success.text: You avoid the spotlight. No consequences.

failure.text: Your absence is seen as guilt. Industry looks bad.

title: The Global Expansion
desc: Expand engineering operations globally
narrative: The company wants to build engineering teams in Tokyo, Berlin, and Bangalore. You need to design the global org structure. Culture and time zones will be challenging.

success.text: Hub coordinates effectively. Spokes have autonomy.

failure.text: Hub becomes a bottleneck. Spokes feel controlled.

success.text: Local teams thrive. Innovation flows everywhere.

failure.text: No coordination. Teams duplicate work.

success.text: Centralized functions provide stability. Local teams ship.

failure.text: Centralization stifles local innovation.

title: The Ethics Committee
desc: Chair the company's AI ethics committee
narrative: Your company's AI products are under scrutiny. The board wants you to chair an ethics committee. You'll set policy for AI development and deployment.

success.text: Guardrails are respected. AI is safe and effective.

failure.text: Guardrails are too strict. Product is uncompetitive.

success.text: Teams move fast. Ethics are built in organically.

failure.text: Something unethical slips through. PR disaster.

success.text: External perspective is valuable. Policy is credible.

failure.text: External ethicists don't understand the tech. Policy is naive.

title: The Acquisition Target
desc: Your company is approached for acquisition
narrative: A tech giant wants to acquire your company. The offer is generous. But what happens to your team? Your culture? Your vision?

success.text: Team is retained. Culture is preserved. Deal closes.

failure.text: Deal closes. Team is absorbed. Key people leave.

success.text: Company thrives independently. You're vindicated.

failure.text: Company struggles without the acquisition capital.

success.text: Cultural protections hold. Best of both worlds.

failure.text: Cultural protections are ignored. You're powerless.

title: The Industry Standard
desc: Propose an industry-wide technical standard
narrative: You've been asked to lead the effort to create an industry standard for your domain. This is prestigious but politically complex. Competitors will resist.

success.text: Your tech becomes the standard. Market dominance.

failure.text: Competitors form a coalition against you. You lose.

success.text: Neutral standard is adopted. You're the hero.

failure.text: Standard is too generic. Nobody adopts it.

success.text: Your tech wins organically. No politics needed.

failure.text: Competitor's tech wins. You're irrelevant.

title: The Succession Crisis
desc: The CEO is stepping down unexpectedly
narrative: The CEO has resigned abruptly. The board is looking for a successor. You're one of three candidates. The other two are external hires with more business experience.

success.text: You win the CEO role. Engineering perspective valued.

failure.text: You lose to an external hire. Your influence wanes.

success.text: Your chosen candidate wins. You're the power behind the throne.

failure.text: Your candidate loses. You're sidelined.

success.text: You focus on engineering. New CEO respects your domain.

failure.text: New CEO doesn't value engineering. Your influence drops.

title: The Technical Memoir
desc: Write a book about your engineering career
narrative: Your publisher wants you to write a memoir about your engineering journey. It could cement your legacy — or expose company secrets.

success.text: Book is a bestseller. You're a thought leader.

failure.text: Book exposes too much. Legal threatens action.

success.text: Book is safe but forgettable.

failure.text: Readers see through the sanitization. Reputation suffers.

success.text: You avoid the risk. Your work speaks for itself.

failure.text: Rival writes a better book. You're forgotten.

title: The Open Source Foundation
desc: Found an open-source foundation
narrative: You want to create a foundation to steward critical open-source projects. This is prestigious but requires significant fundraising and governance design.

success.text: Foundation is well-governed. Projects thrive.

failure.text: Governance is flawed. Projects fracture.

success.text: Foundation grows organically. Sustainable.

failure.text: Foundation never gains traction. Wasted effort.

success.text: Partner provides infrastructure. You focus on projects.

failure.text: Partner's politics slow everything down.

title: The Boardroom Coup
desc: A faction on the board wants to oust the CEO
narrative: A group of board members wants to replace the CEO. They want your vote. This is corporate politics at its most dangerous.

success.text: CEO stays. Stability preserved.

failure.text: CEO is ousted anyway. You're seen as weak.

success.text: New CEO is better. Company turns around.

failure.text: New CEO is worse. Company declines.

success.text: You avoid the fallout. No enemies made.

failure.text: Both sides see you as unreliable.

title: The Legacy Codebase
desc: A 30-year-old system must be replaced
narrative: Your company's core system was written in COBOL in 1994. It processes 90% of transactions. It's held together by duct tape and the memories of retired engineers.

success.text: Rewrite succeeds. System is fast and maintainable.

failure.text: Rewrite fails. System crashes. Revenue plummets.

success.text: Gradual migration. Zero downtime. Success.

failure.text: Migration is too slow. Legacy system collapses mid-way.

success.text: It works. For now.

failure.text: System crashes. Catastrophic failure.

title: The Venture Capital Offer
desc: A VC wants to invest — with conditions
narrative: A top-tier VC wants to invest $100M. But they want board control, a faster growth path, and your resignation as CTO if the company is sold.

success.text: Investment accelerates growth. You stay on.

failure.text: VC forces your resignation. You're out.

success.text: You get favorable terms. Investment closes.

failure.text: VC walks away. You lost a great opportunity.

success.text: Company grows organically. You maintain control.

failure.text: Competitor takes the VC money. You fall behind.

title: The Nobel Prize Nomination
desc: You're nominated for a Nobel Prize in Computer Science
narrative: Your contributions to distributed systems have earned you a Nobel nomination. The ceremony is in Stockholm. This is the pinnacle of academic recognition.

success.text: Speech inspires a generation. You're a legend.

failure.text: Speech is too technical. Audience is lost.

success.text: You keep the honor. No performance required.

failure.text: Declining the ceremony is seen as arrogant.

success.text: You avoid the spotlight. No regrets.

failure.text: Nomination is withdrawn. You look ungrateful.

title: BOSS: The Ultimate Merger
desc: The final boss: merge with the industry's largest competitor
narrative: The biggest merger in tech history. Two giants become one. You're tasked with integrating the engineering organizations. 10,000 engineers. Two cultures. One deadline.

success.text: You absorb them cleanly. New company is stronger.

failure.text: Absorption fails. Culture clash destroys both teams.

success.text: New culture is authentic. Everyone embraces it.

failure.text: New culture is incoherent. Nobody adopts it.

success.text: Market rewards the merger. Stock soars.

failure.text: Market punishes the merger. Stock crashes.
